brief: For MK A3, the durable monitoring backbone is narrow but high quality: NBStat (nbstat.nbrm.mk) is a genuine PxWeb database with a standard API covering monetary, external and financial-accounts series, and ENER (ener.gov.mk) is the statutory consultation register that carries draft financial-sector laws and their comment deadlines before anything reaches the Official Gazette (slvesnik.com.mk), which remains the legally binding dating mechanism and offers a free-issue tier plus a queryable archived-issues index. The weak link is push notification and provenance: no RSS/e-mail alert endpoint could be confirmed anywhere on nbrm.mk, the site returns 403 to automated fetchers (bot-defended, not dead), data.gov.mk refused connection on the single attempt, and web.archive.org was unreachable from this agent — so archive depth for the regulator estate is asserted, never measured. Practical consequence: this cell should be operationalised as poll-plus-snapshot (crawl the NBRM supervision, reporting-obligation and register pages in browser context, hash every linked PDF, and push each new document to Wayback ourselves) rather than assuming existing archives already hold the version history. Two mechanical wins remain unclaimed and cheap: a feed-probe sweep (sitemap.xml, /feed, /wp-json) across the .gov.mk estate, and CDX indexing of commercial-bank tariff and general-conditions pages built off the NBRM bank register.
